teams.synopsis: The best team on paper after the draft — Chubb and Jacobs make this RB duo tough to beat.
teams.blurb:
• Top 7 QB
  • Two top 10 RBs
  • Two potential mid-high end WR2s
  • Top 7 TE
  • Weak FLEX

I don't believe any team sticks out as the top team this early, but I believe this team has the best team on paper after the draft. The RB duo of Chubb and Jacobs will make this team difficult to beat every week.

teams.synopsis: An RB-heavy roster with real depth — a healthy Hall could make trades unnecessary.
teams.blurb:
• Potential top 7 QB
  • One low end RB1 and three mid-high end RB2s
  • Elite WR1 but lacks a strong WR2
  • Very weak TE position

This team lacks receiving depth, but the abundance of running backs makes future trades for a WR2/TE inevitable. If Hall can return to his pre-injury self, then this team might not even have to make trades to be dominant.

teams.synopsis: One of the best WR duos in the league — but it all rides on Javonte's health.
teams.blurb:
• Top 3 QB
  • Solidified RB1 but questions around RB2
  • One of the best WR duos in the league
  • Average TE
  • Weak FLEX as of now but Addison has potential

If this team can stay healthy and perform close to their potential, then they'll be dangerous. A lot rides on the back of Javonte Williams and how he'll play after last year's ACL injury.

teams.synopsis: Could easily be ranked #1 after Week 1 — no weak spots if JSN can produce.
teams.blurb:
• Top 7 QB
  • Two top 15 RBs
  • Elite WR1 and a mid-low end WR2
  • Top 4 TE
  • Weak FLEX as of now but JSN has potential

This team can easily be ranked #1 after week one, but as of now I think #4 is a good spot. If JSN can at least be a low-end WR2, this team will have no weak spots and be very scary.

teams.synopsis: The most well-rounded team in the league — the best TE in fantasy covers for a shaky QB.
teams.blurb:
• Below average QB
  • Solid RB duo but Dobbins staying healthy is a concern
  • Low-end WR1 and low-end WR2
  • Best TE gives massive advantage
  • Slightly above average FLEX

This is the most well-rounded team with no weaknesses besides Dak at QB, and even then, he'll be good for a few top-5 finishes.

teams.synopsis: The league's best WR duo — a healthy Tua and a breakout Sanders could make this scary.
teams.blurb:
• Below average QB
  • Extremely weak RB duo
  • Best WR duo in the league, both could be top 5
  • Above average TE with upside
  • One of, if not the best FLEX in the league

If Sanders can establish himself as a top 10-15 RB in fantasy and Tua can stay healthy and produce, then this team will be very scary week in and week out.

teams.synopsis: Strong at receiver, but the RB2 hole and QB question mark could hold this team back.
teams.blurb:
• Below average QB
  • Mid-tier RB1 but one of the worst RB2 in the league
  • Two WRs that can finish top 10
  • Top 4 TE
  • Average FLEX

This team excels at the receiving positions but lacks a true RB2 and great QB. It will be important to watch how Ridley and Cook play this year.

teams.synopsis: If the RB2 and flex spots sort themselves out, this team could be a top-3 threat.
teams.blurb:
• Top 3 QB
  • High-end RB1 but low-end RB2
  • Mid-tier WR1 and WR2
  • Top 7 TE
  • Weak FLEX

If this team can figure out its RB2 and FLEX situation it could be scary. Additionally, Skyy Moore and Khalil Herbert in bigger roles this year may give this team the added boost it needs to be top 3.

teams.synopsis: A boom-or-bust roster — Gibbs and Hopkins will define this team's ceiling.
teams.blurb:
• Potential top 7 QB
  • Elite RB1 and high-end RB2
  • WR duo has question marks, but both have potential to be top 15
  • Top 7 TE
  • Above average FLEX

This team has a lot of players that can be boom or bust, like Gibbs and Hopkins, which makes it interesting to pay attention to them through the first month of the season.

teams.synopsis: The best QB in the league and an elite RB duo — but the WRs are a total unknown.
teams.blurb:
• Best QB in the league
  • RB duo is elite, both have potential to finish top 3
  • Weak and unproven WR duo
  • Average TE
  • Average/Below Average FLEX

This team has the tools to be top 3 in the league, but it depends on how Higgins, London, and Aiyuk play this season. Also, the JT situation is something to watch.

teams.synopsis: A ceiling that depends entirely on Kupp — and on White and Watson taking the next step.
teams.blurb:
• Average QB
  • Two mid-low end RB2s
  • WR1 can finish as the best WR in the league and high-end WR2
  • Average TE
  • Average FLEX

If Kupp can stay healthy and return to form this team has a chance to be pretty good, but it depends on White and Watson taking the next jump.

teams.synopsis: Elite at QB and WR, but a preseason trade left this roster thin at RB.
teams.blurb:
• Top 7 QB
  • Weak RB duo, unless Mattison proves himself
  • Elite WR duo, both can finish top 10
  • Very weak TE
  • Average FLEX

The QB and WR duo are elite, but the rest of the team seems like it could be mediocre or disappointing. The preseason trade made this team weak at RB, but hopefully (for this team) Mattison finishes as a top 10-15 RB.

teams.synopsis: Three 'averages' in one profile, but a returning Kamara could change the whole outlook.
teams.blurb:
• Average QB
  • Mid-tier RB1 but w/out Kamara for 3 weeks makes the RB2 very weak
  • One of the best WR duos in the league
  • Average TE
  • Average FLEX

Using the word 'average' three times when describing a team is never ideal, but add to that an RB2 that's very weak, and that's what led this team to being ranked #13. Still, if Kamara returns to form, this team could be dangerous.

teams.synopsis: An elite RB1 undercut by the worst RB2 in the league — the Cook signing is the swing factor.
teams.blurb:
• Top 7 QB
  • Elite RB1 but the RB2 is the worst in the league w/out Cook being signed
  • Average WR duo
  • Top 4 TE
  • Below average FLEX

The hole at RB2, mixed with the uncertainty of MT, is what dragged this team down to #14, but if things go this team's way and the players live up to their potential, then this team can be nice.
